Subject: Onramp: SDK environment checklist, sample apps & local test plan

Hi Ariel — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the technical deep dive next week.

Summary from today's discovery:
- BrightWave will run a pilot for a content-generation flow and an embeddings-based semantic search.
- Goals: sub-second median latency for short prompts, embeddings with ~10M doc index and reranker in the loop.
- Compliance: you mentioned SOC2 and a preference for private VPC for production.

What we will deliver before the tech deep dive (target: 2 business days):
1) A short one-pager (attached) summarizing recommended SDK path and auth options.
2) SDK quickstart guides (Python + TypeScript) with local Docker testing instructions (rdw-sdk-quickstart.md attached).
3) Two sample apps: (a) generator sample, (b) embeddings + reranker sample (repo link in next email).
4) Reference routing & structured-output config for tool calling and reranking (we'll include a sample YAML).

Questions / asks for BrightWave:
- Which environment do you want to test locally first? (mac/linux dev workstation or Linux container in CI)
- Who should I invite from engineering for the deep-dive? I saw Marcus on the invite list — can you confirm?

Proposed next step: tech deep-dive on Tue 2026-12-08 11:00 PT — if that works I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda and pre-reads.

Attachments: onramp-summary.pdf, rdw-sdk-quickstart.md

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Auth: our security lead prefers OIDC for production (we use Okta), but for the pilot we'd like a local-friendly option (API key or Docker-based credentials). Can you outline the tradeoffs?
2) SDKs: Python is the primary dev path but we have a small frontend team that wants a TypeScript example (server-side Node). Please prioritize both.
3) Local testing: we run most of our CI in GitHub Actions and devs work on mac/linux. Docker-compose for local emulation would be ideal.

Confirming Marcus (marcus.lin@brightwave.com) is the engineering lead — include him on the deep dive invite. Also please loop in security contact for SOC2/Q&A.

Appreciate it — Ariel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Onramp: quick notes on auth/routing/embeddings for BrightWave

Vanessa / Rachel — quick technical notes I drafted to include in the consolidated reply: 

Auth options (pilot -> prod):
- Pilot: API key with scoped permissions + token rotation script. Easy for local and CI.
- Pilot (alternate): short-lived OIDC tokens via Okta (we have an example using oidc-client in the samples).
- Prod (BrightWave private): Mutual TLS or OIDC with dedicated client_id + mTLS for token exchange; KMS integration for keys.

Routing and model selection:
- Route by latency requirement and cost tier. Example: fast-path -> gptrex-8k-quant (lower cost) for short prompts; fallback -> gptrex-8k-fp32 for quality-sensitive calls.
- We can attach per-route fallback policies in the routing YAML. I'll attach sample-routing-config.yaml.

Structured output / tool calling:
- Recommend using our JSON-schema mode for tool calling. Sample in the TS sample shows a tools registry + schema validation step.

Embeddings & reranker notes:
- Use 1536-d embeddings (default) and HNSW index for pilot; store vector shards in S3 + metadata DB.
- Reranker as a lightweight re-score model called on top-K candidates (we include a reranker wrapper in the samples).

I'll push a minimal reference repo to https://github.com/redwood/rdw-sdks-onramp and attach sample-routing-config.yaml to this thread.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample-routing-config.yaml
